captions.headline: Eighty-three percent of employers will use AI to screen your resume in 2026.
captions.subline: The system reading you is not a person. Write for both.
captions.caption_linkedin:
Eighty-three percent of companies are expected to use AI for resume screening by the end of 2026.

This is the part of job seeking that quietly changed under your feet. A decade ago, the first reader of your CV was a recruiter who took a glance and made a quick judgment. Today, in a majority of applications, the first reader is software that scores your CV against the job description before any human sees it.

The two readers want different things. The software wants explicit keyword matches, clean structure, the title from the job posting echoed back in your summary. The human wants to see a specific person who did specific things at specific places.

The trap most job seekers fall into is writing for one and ignoring the other. Optimize only for the software and a human reader will find your CV stiff and generic. Write only for the human and the software will not surface you to that human in the first place.

The fix is not magic. It is a structural rewrite of the top of your CV per role, with explicit keywords baked into language a real person actually uses. That work takes about twenty minutes per application by hand. Spark Careers does it for you in five.

captions.headline: Complex design is the number one reason resumes fail ATS parsing.
captions.subline: The fancy template that looks impressive is the one the system cannot read.
captions.caption_facebook:
If you bought a beautifully designed resume template from one of the freelance marketplaces, here is information you need.

Resume formatting research from 2026 finds that complex visual design is the number one reason a CV fails to parse correctly in an Applicant Tracking System. Multi-column layouts, sidebars, decorative icons, header graphics, and unusual fonts all reduce the chance that the system reads your work history in the order you wrote it.

The template that looks impressive on your laptop screen is often the one that arrives at the recruiter as a scrambled wall of text.

The rule that holds up across every parser: one column. One simple font. Clear section headings. Standard bullet points. The visual hierarchy that helps a human eye scan is the same hierarchy the parser is looking for.

Spark Careers builds CVs in the format that passes parsers, then lets you customize the wording per role. The plain version is the version that gets through.

captions.headline: Sixty-eight percent of HR teams want two pages, not one.
captions.subline: The one-page rule expired. Use the space the role earns.
captions.caption_linkedin:
The advice you got in college, about keeping your resume to one page, is officially behind the curve.

A 2026 survey of HR professionals found that sixty-eight percent now prefer a two-page resume for experienced candidates over a cramped one-page version. The cramped one-page CV used to signal discipline. It now signals that you are hiding something or trying too hard to compress a real career into the format your career services office insisted on in 2014.

This is good news for anybody with more than five years of experience, anybody who took a non-linear path, anybody who switched industries, anybody who had to explain a career break, anybody who has built skills that do not fit on one page in eight-point font.

Use the space the role earns. If your second page is genuine, useful, and easy to scan, recruiters will read it.

The rule that still holds: every line of the CV has to earn its place. Two pages is permission, not an obligation.

captions.headline: Every right hire frees an hour. Every wrong hire costs four.
captions.subline: Recruitment is the only function in your business with leveraged math.
captions.caption_linkedin:
There is one function in a small business where the math breaks in your favor.

It is hiring.

Every other function trades current time for current output. Sales trades hours for revenue. Operations trades hours for delivery. Bookkeeping trades hours for compliance. The line is flat. You work the hours. You get the result.

Hiring is different. A well-made hire does not just do the work today. They do the work tomorrow, next month, next quarter. They take ten hours off your week, every week, indefinitely. They unblock the things you cannot get to because you are doing the thing they should be doing.

The catch runs the other direction with equal force. A wrong hire costs the same way. Four hours a week, every week, while you keep the wrong fit on the team because the cost of replacing them feels higher than the cost of tolerating them. It usually is not.

So treat hiring with the seriousness of the only function that compounds. Take it slow at the start. Reply fast. Reference check. Trust the second instinct.

Keep going.

captions.headline: Four thousand tech jobs were cut this week. IT postings overall are up fourteen percent year over year.
captions.subline: The market is shifting, not shrinking. Where you apply matters as much as how.
captions.caption_linkedin:
Two numbers worth holding in the same hand this week.

This week alone, the layoff trackers added more than four thousand tech workers to the count. Amdocs let go of about 2,900. Salesforce trimmed roughly 86 across Agentforce, Mulesoft, and Marketing Cloud. The news cycle that comes with that count is heavy if you are reading it from inside the affected segment.

The second number, from the same period, tells a different story. IT and computer science job postings overall rose 14.2 percent year over year through April 2026. Companies are cutting from specific functions (customer support, content moderation, data entry, QA testing, traditional software engineering) and reinvesting the saved budget into AI infrastructure, data center capacity, and the next generation of tooling.

Both things are true. The market is not shrinking. The market is shifting.

For a job seeker, that has practical implications. Where you apply, and how you frame your experience for the segment that is actually growing, matters as much as how many applications you send. The CV that worked for the role you held in 2023 will not necessarily work for the role that exists in 2026.

Spark Careers reframes your CV around the capability the next role is asking for, not the chair you sat in. Free. https://spark.risepointcareers.com/?utm_source=social&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=w26-thu-b2c
